$comment: A VERSION is {music, edit, sfxSet} — the three things that together decide what a master is. It exists because the edit snaps to the music's downbeats and the cue sheet is derived from the resulting cut, so changing any one of them changes the film. ONE flat map, not two: an audition is a version with somewhere else to write and a reason it may not ship, which is two fields, not a second namespace. `FILM_VERSION` selects an entry and everything else — music, edit, sfx set, output directory — follows from it. Nothing here is derived.
$auditionNote: The `+el` versions use `elevenlabs-audition`, generated on a free ElevenLabs plan and carrying commercialUse: false. They render at FULL master quality — same codec, same loudness target — because the founder judges finished films, but `npm run verify:release` routes them to their own outDir and refuses to let them into out/masters/. See docs/audio-provenance.md §4.

$quality.master: Identical to a release master: H.264, crf 18, yuv420p, AAC 192k, -16 LUFS +/-0.5, true peak <= -1.0 dBTP. An audition that looks or sounds cheaper than the real thing is not an audition of the real thing.
$quality.$loudnessNote: verify:loudness must pass per version. Watch the first 64 ms: the 60s A master measured -1.2 dBTP there, where the bed's entry meets the opening cue. The opening cue's gain is the dial, not the bed's.

A-confident-arrival.note: Rendered, approved, and re-renderable byte for byte. Its resolved timeline is locked in edit-a-timeline.lock.json.

B-daylight-forward.note: Re-arranged around the second take: brighter, faster, every major boundary on a measured downbeat.

A-confident-arrival+el.note: Version A's picture and take, with the ElevenLabs palette. The draw cue is EQ'd for A's darker bed — see sfx-roles.json perMusic.

B-daylight-forward+el.note: The B edit with the ElevenLabs palette. Unblocked: edit B exists now, and this entry resolves through the same map as every other version.
